rule: Requests are intentionally narrow. Do not ask for 'all UFO/UAP records' when an exact archive object, date, unit, data product, or disposition question is available.

requests.destination_type: NARA reference inquiry / Modern Military or UAP reference
requests.subject: Project Blue Book RB-47 case, 17 July 1957 — exact file-unit/item NAID and digital object URLs
requests.request_body: I am trying to resolve the Project Blue Book case concerning the RB-47 electronic reconnaissance aircraft event of 17 July 1957 to its exact NARA Catalog file-unit/item identity. NARA's official UAP bulk-download page identifies Project Blue Book Case Files series NAID 595466 and sanitized series 597821. Non-NARA discovery indexes point to Project Blue Book case 4810, T-1206 roll 1 index page NARA-PBB1-167, and a possible archive reference 6961835. I am not asking NARA to validate those external identifiers. Could you please provide the exact NARA file-unit/item NAID(s), Catalog URL(s), and available digital-object/file URLs for the 17 July 1957 RB-47 case, and indicate whether the associated item contains only case paperwork or any original radar/ELINT recording media or instrument data?
success_fields: statement whether original sensor media/data are present

requests.destination_type: Department of the Navy FOIA / records-management routing
requests.subject: USS Princeton CG-59 November 2004 — applicable records schedule and disposition for Aegis/CIC track-history records
requests.request_body: This request is limited to records-management provenance, not a renewed request for the underlying UAP sensor data. For USS Princeton (CG-59) during 10-16 November 2004, please identify the records schedule/SSIC and disposition authority that governed: (1) AN/SPY-1/Aegis track-history or tactical target data, (2) Combat Information Center tactical/event logs, (3) any exercise-monitoring electronic video/data used for event reconstruction, and (4) air-defense-control-net or comparable tactical communications recordings. If available, please provide any records-transfer, destruction, disposition, or retention-exception documentation for those data classes for USS Princeton or the relevant carrier strike group/exercise. Historical NARA schedule N1-NU-89-005 lists SSIC 3560/1 Combat Information Center Logs as temporary, but this request does not assume raw SPY-1 products were classified under that item. I am asking for the exact 2004 mapping and disposition authority.
success_fields: exception or permanent-retention rule if applicable

requests.subject: Tehran 18-21 September 1976 — RG59 CFPF / USDAO / military-advisory records concerning F-4 intercept and equipment faults
requests.request_body: I am researching records surrounding the Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 intercept reported in the contemporaneous U.S. DIA/JCS message for 19 September 1976. I am specifically seeking primary records beyond the already released narrative message. Could you identify RG59 Central Foreign Policy Files (NAID 654098), indexed microfilm, Foreign Service Post, USDAO, ARMISH/MAAG, or related U.S. advisory records dated 18-21 September 1976 that concern Tehran/Mehrabad/Shahrokhi, F-4 interceptor operations, radar contacts, communications/instrument failures, maintenance/fault reports, or follow-up reporting? For any hits, please provide MRN/document number, date, from/to, subject, film/index identifier, and digital image or ordering reference. I am particularly interested in maintenance/fault or radar/communications records that could independently test the reported instrumentation effects and geometry.

do_not_infer: No Records Located means the record never existed
A short retention schedule proves a specific sensor record was destroyed
An official case file proves extraordinary physics
A precise narrative number is calibrated measurement
canonical_seal: R5 ASKS FOR IDENTIFIERS, DATA PRODUCTS, AND DISPOSITION — NOT FOR BETTER UFO STORIES.
